name: mpc
reason: No numeric comparison against any baseline. README (opened) has no benchmark section; repo has only examples/ and tests/. Issue #35 'Parsing is extremely slow' (opened) holds only self-timings by a user (empty input 0.9 s per 10,000 iterations on a 1 GHz x86; 8-line input 54.4 s per 10,000 iterations) and concludes too slow for production; no lex/yacc or other baseline. README only says mpc_predictive/mpc_optimise help performance, no numbers. Web searches found no shootout that includes mpc.

name: OpenXLSX
listed_description: A C++ library for reading, writing, creating and modifying Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) files.
reason: Numbers but no baseline. README Performance section gives OpenXLSX-only Google Benchmark output (about 4,000,000 cells per second, 8.38861M items, 16 x 2300 MHz CPU) and itself says it is severely outdated as of 2026-04-19. Benchmarks/Benchmark.cpp includes only OpenXLSX.hpp and benchmark.h; the dated Benchmarks/ subdirectories are before/after regression runs of itself. Issues #198 and #350 report slow reads/writes with no comparison to xlnt, libxlsxwriter or any other library. No third-party shootout found.

name: owl
listed_description: A parser generator for visibly pushdown languages.
reason: Directional claim only: README says generated parsers always run in linear time and lists memory use and large grammars as limitations; no numbers and no baseline. A University of Twente thesis ('Performance Testing Owl, Parser Generator for Visibly Pushdown Grammars', Luc Timmerman, 2022, purl.utwente.nl/essays/91958) tests Owl's performance claims and reports some were incorrect, but purl.utwente.nl and essay.utwente.nl are EGRESS_BLOCKED here and the search snippet gives no numbers or baselines, so it could not be read.

name: Pawn.Regex
listed_description: A Pawn plugin that provides support for regular expressions using C++11 std::regex.
reason: No numbers. README only claims it is better than other Pawn regex plugins because it exposes match groups (a feature claim, not speed). Repo has cmake/, lib/, src/ only; no benchmark. Web search found no comparison.

name: rapidcsv
listed_description: An easy-to-use, header-only C++ CSV parser library.
reason: Makes no speed claim and no baseline numbers in README, repo (tests/, no benchmark dir) or issues (#15 'rapidcsv is not that rapid!' only reports a 2x gain on Visual Studio 2017 from cell += buffer[i] instead of cell = cell + buffer[i], a self comparison; #95 has no numbers). Only numbers found are third-party and show rapidcsv as the slower side: vincentlaucsb/csv-parser benchmarks/README.md (i5-12400, MSVC 19.50, C++20, AVX2, Google Benchmark 1.8.5) 500K clean rows load 244.7 ms rapidcsv vs 156.7 ms csv-parser, load+save 683.0 ms vs 310.5 ms; 5M clean load 2,587 ms vs 666.3 ms. That is a competitor first-party benchmark where rapidcsv loses, so no record.

name: restclient-cpp
listed_description: Simple REST client for C++. It wraps libcurl for HTTP requests.
reason: No numbers and no performance claim. README describes a thin libcurl wrapper (connection reuse via curl handle keep-alive, no benchmark). Issue search for performance found nothing with numbers. Web search found no shootout including restclient-cpp.

name: semver.c
listed_description: A semver parser and render in ANSI C.
reason: No numbers and no performance claim. README documents API only; repo contains semver.c, semver.h, semver_test.c, semver_unit.c and no benchmark. Web search found no shootout including semver.c.
